A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–F. Their contents can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v2 reports original linear-regression experiments on synthetic data in Figure 1 and California Housing data in Appendix F, Figure 2.

after.justification: v3 retains the original synthetic-data experiments in Figure 1 and California Housing experiments in Appendix F, Figure 2.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1 and 2 retain the same optimization procedures, output perturbation, and robust trimmed-mean training. Removing the SGD qualifier from Figure 1a does not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate synthetic linear regression with in-distribution and label-shifted out-of-distribution forget data, plus out-of-distribution unlearning on California Housing. No dataset or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Figure 1a still compares Algorithm 1 against DP-SGD. Figure 1b and Figure 2 still compare Algorithms 1 and 2. The analytical comparison methods in the tables also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The captions and Appendix F retain the same sample sizes, forget fractions, label-shift construction, unlearning budgets, optimization budgets, and evaluation metrics. No revised experimental protocol is documented.

E4.justification: The dimensionality study and convergence comparisons across forget-set sizes are retained, including the California Housing validation. No ablation, robustness test, or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The uncertainty-reporting practice is unchanged; revisions to theoretical sub-Gaussian bounds belong to T1.

E6.justification: Table 2 corrects Algorithm 1's non-Lipschitz out-of-distribution computational deletion capacity from 'Unbounded' to '0'. This changes a reported theoretical result entry. The empirical curve values and findings in Figures 1 and 2 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Proposition 1 and Appendix B receive a localized proof correction: population-risk bounds now use distance decompositions around the population minimizer, replacing an invalid smoothness step at empirical minimizers. Lemma 4 becomes a squared-distance bound and drops its smoothness assumption. Equations (4)–(6) revise constants and replace ln(n) with ln(n+1); Appendix C adjusts corresponding coefficients. The main theorem scopes and asymptotic rates remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about dimension-independent in-distribution deletion capacity, separation from differential privacy, worst-case out-of-distribution failure, and robust training with near-linear complexity.

C2.justification: The explanations involving initialization error, robust training, and retain-set interpolation error are unchanged. Section 5's added zero-capacity clause makes explicit the already-stated worst-case failure to unlearn even one sample, without introducing a new limitation or interpretation.

D1.justification: Figure 1a changes 'Alg. 1 w/ SGD' to 'Alg. 1', removing the explicit optimizer identification for that experiment. Appendix F's implementation settings otherwise remain unchanged, and no replacement optimizer is documented.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, cited works, and novelty positioning remain unchanged. References moving between pages 10–12 are retained entries, not additions or removals.

P1.justification: v3 adds a first-page correction notice, expands acknowledgments, and revises local proof explanations and a sentence in Section 5. The overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1a changes curve colors, removes point markers, and shortens and relocates its legend while preserving its data and axes. The correction notice, acknowledgments, and revised equations also cause limited layout and reference reflow.

improvement.justification: v3 repairs the invalid smoothness argument supporting Proposition 1 and corrects Table 2's misleading capacity entry, improving mathematical reliability. The correction remains incomplete: Appendix E, page 25, still applies Proposition 1 with the old coefficients. Figure 1a also loses its explicit SGD identification. These changes provide a clear but limited net improvement.
